title: Atomically record released attempt and provider-slot state
description: Corrective producer prerequisite for task-e62e3828df234c66969a99b8223487f4. Hard-depend on task-2db110998677498abb11f65142a6fe25, task-740924b741754955b94a7ccf7fc16bb1 and task-4731ba34d3b3463685dccd325a11f325. Current live bytes contradict core safe-release: `attempt-release-disposition.ts` copies activation `attempt.state` (`RUNNING`) and provider slot `state` (`ACTIVE`) even when `releaseWork` returns RELEASED; `releaseProviderSlot` has zero daemon production callers. At the same release composition point, derive the exact slot-release command from the decision-verified activation slot/attempt, invoke the public scheduler transition, and persist its successor together with the scheduler release outcome in the one AttemptReleaseRecorded decision. The release row's `attemptState` is the safe-boundary transaction outcome (`DRAINING` or `RELEASED`), not the earlier activation slice. No second event/partial authority may survive a slot refusal. This task does not supply safe-boundary, terminal, receipt or handoff evidence; those remain separate producers.
definitionOfDone: When the scheduler release outcome is RELEASED, the daemon derives a provider-slot release command only from the durable activation slot and attempt, calls public `releaseProviderSlot`, and persists the returned exact slot ref/state; no caller slot state or command is accepted.

The same single AttemptReleaseRecorded body records `attemptState === "RELEASED"`, `leaseState === "RELEASED"`, and `providerSlotState === "RELEASED"`; DRAINING records the kernel's DRAINING attempt/lease outcome and retains the non-released slot without claiming safe release.

A malformed, mismatched, RESERVED, or otherwise refused slot transition preserves the scheduler code under a distinct provider-slot-release layer and commits zero release rows/decisions; it is never restamped as a lease-drain refusal.
Replay returns the original durable row with unchanged raw event/decision counts; conflicting bytes or a later divergent slot fact refuse before a second write.

Real SqliteEventStore tests seed activation only through the production activation path, assert exact code/layer and one accepted released composition, and read all three states from canonical durable bytes rather than the input/result echo.
Mutations that copy activation RUNNING into `attemptState` or hardcode/skip the provider-slot successor each redden a named production-surface assertion.
`pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` run separately with a nonzero count line and no owned-path regression.
taskRails: Own only apps/daemon/src/work/attempt-release-disposition.ts, attempt-release-store.ts, and attempt-release-disposition.test.ts; do not edit activation-ledger state, scheduler reducers, schemas, RuntimeCommandKind or the current-reader task.
Hard-depend on task-2db110998677498abb11f65142a6fe25; consume `releaseProviderSlot` only from bare `@moe/scheduler`, with manifest+lock+compiled-probe edge verified before implementation.
The release decision is all-or-none: a slot refusal leaves no release row, and DRAINING never upgrades attempt or slot to RELEASED.
This task does not accept or manufacture safeBoundaryObserved, terminal refs/flags, receiptRef or handoff; those remain tasks ded026d6, 6d400781 and af9454f4.
